baslik: In the Land of the Wet Nurse
ozet: Thuwayba and Halima; blessings in the land of the Banu Sa'd; weaning; the opening of the chest; the return to Mecca.

b04-s01: After his birth, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was nursed for a while by Thuwayba, a servant of Abu Lahab.

Meccan families gave their children to wet nurses from the Bedouin tribes, so that they would grow up in the healthy air of the desert and learn pure Arabic. 'Abd al-Muttalib, too, looked for a wet nurse for his grandson.
b04-s02: The wet nurse was Halima, of the Sa'd ibn Bakr branch of the Hawazin tribe. Her husband was al-Harith; their children 'Abdullah, Unaysa and Shayma would become the Prophet's foster brother and sisters.
As Halima related, there was a famine that year. With her husband and the son she was nursing, she set out for Mecca together with the women of the Banu Sa'd who were looking for children to nurse.
The grey donkey she rode was weak, and the old she-camel with them gave not a drop of milk. Her son cried with hunger, so they could not sleep at night.
b04-s03: In Mecca the Prophet was offered to each of the women. When they heard he was an orphan, none of them took him, for they hoped for a reward from the child's father.
Every woman except Halima found a child to nurse. Halima did not want to go back empty-handed and told her husband that she would take that orphan.
Her husband said: «Perhaps Allah will give us a blessing through him.»
b04-s04: As Halima related, when she took him, her milk became plentiful; both he and his foster brother drank their fill and slept.
Her husband went to milk the old she-camel, and she had given milk. That night they slept in peace.
In the morning her husband said: «By Allah, Halima, you have taken a blessed soul.»
b04-s05: On the way back, Halima's weak donkey left the whole company behind.
The land of the Banu Sa'd was among the driest. Yet in the evenings Halima's sheep came home full and heavy with milk, while the sheep of others came home hungry.
b04-s06: The Prophet grew quickly, not like other children. At two he was weaned.
Halima brought him to his mother; but because of the blessing he brought, she very much wanted him to stay with them.
Saying she feared the sickness in Mecca, she asked Amina's permission to keep him until he grew stronger. At Halima's insistence, Amina agreed.
b04-s07: While the Prophet was with his wet nurse, one day as he was playing with the children, Gabriel came to him.
He laid him on the ground, opened his chest and took out his heart; he removed a clot of blood from it and said: «This was Satan's share of you.»
Then he washed the heart with Zamzam water in a golden basin, closed it and put it back in its place.
b04-s08: The children ran to his wet nurse and said: «Muhammad has been killed!»
When they reached him, his colour had faded. Anas ibn Malik says that he saw the mark of that stitching on his chest.
b04-s09: After this, Halima and her husband feared that something might happen to him, and they took him back to his family.
According to the reports, when Halima brought him to Mecca, she lost him in the upper part of the town and told 'Abd al-Muttalib.
'Abd al-Muttalib stood by the Ka'ba and prayed to Allah that he be found. Waraqa ibn Nawfal and a man of Quraysh found him and brought him back.
'Abd al-Muttalib lifted him onto his shoulder, walked around the Ka'ba praying, and then sent him to his mother Amina.
b04-s10: Amina asked Halima why they had brought him. At first Halima did not want to say; when Amina insisted, she told her what had happened.
Amina said: Satan had no way to him; this son of hers had a great future.
The Prophet had stayed with his wet nurse until he was four or five years old.
